options: All points the same distance from a center
A shape with four equal straight sides
A shape with three straight sides
questions.explanation: A circle is every point at one fixed distance from its center.
questions.misconception: Four sides make a square and three make a triangle — the circle is defined by equal distance from a center, not sides.

questions.prompt: If a circle's diameter is 10 cm, what is its radius?
questions.explanation: The diameter is two radii, so the radius is 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm.
questions.misconception: The diameter crosses the whole circle — the radius is half of it, not the same or double.

options: The distance around the rim of the circle
The distance from center to rim
questions.explanation: Circumference is the total distance around the outside edge.
questions.misconception: Center-to-rim is the radius and across-through-center is the diameter — around the outside is the circumference.

questions.prompt: For ANY circle, circumference divided by diameter equals...
questions.explanation: The ratio of circumference to diameter is always pi, no matter the circle's size.
questions.misconception: Pi is a constant ratio — bigger circles have bigger absolute numbers but the ratio stays the same ~3.14.

questions.prompt: A wheel with radius 1 unit rolls one full turn. How far does it travel?
questions.explanation: One turn covers one circumference = 2 × π × r = 2 × π × 1 ≈ 6.28 units.
questions.misconception: The wheel travels its circumference per turn, which is 2πr — the radius alone or the diameter alone is too small.
